chunks.rationale: Two renderer cases prove the contract without an App-level mount. test/sidebar.test.tsx: after scoping to p2 via the existing picker helpers, clicking [data-view-nav=planboard] delivers that id to onOpenPlanboard; unscoped click delivers null. test/planboardView.test.tsx: initialProjectId=p2 loads /tmp/site and sets the <select> to p2; changing the select to p1 still refetches /tmp/ledger, so the in-view selector still wins.
risks: No App integration test that openPlanboard writes planboardProjectId and PlanboardView receives it. The glue is three lines; a missed prop would still typecheck only because PlanboardViewProps now declares initialProjectId.

chunks.rationale: Sidebar widens onOpenPlanboard to (scopedProjectId?: string | null) and passes projectScope from the Planboard nav button. App stores that id in planboardProjectId and hands it to PlanboardView as initialProjectId. PlanboardView seeds useState from the prop and an effect keyed only on initialProjectId updates it when the prop changes (re-click while already on the board). App always passes string | null (never omits the prop), so the effect's !== undefined guard is true on every PlanboardView mount; user select still wins because a later select change does not change initialProjectId.
risks: Re-clicking Planboard with the same sidebar scope while the board is already open does not reset the in-view select (planboardProjectId is unchanged, effect does not fire). Spec says the user select must win; a product owner who expected 'nav click re-applies scope' would see the previous select instead.
When scope is All projects, projectScope is null, PlanboardView falls back to projects[0] — same as today, now explicit.
Kanban and Activity nav still ignore sidebar scope (offered as a follow-up chip, not this diff).
